newsitem.title: USA: GAP shares down on flat same-store sales. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GAP shares down on flat same-store sales. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]

text.p: NEW YORK, Sep 4 (Reuter) Shares of GAP Inc sold off 4-7/8 to 29 and topped the New York Stock Exchange's most active list on Thursday after the company reported flat same store sales for August, analysts said.
"Their overall sales are up, but same store sales are flat and that could be a precursor of poor earnings," said Hildergard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities.
The company said that overall sales rose 19 percent in August while same store sales were unchanged.

"I think this in keeping with what GAP has done on a regular basis. It does seem to trade in a much wider range than most retailers," said Dick Stein, vice-president at U.S. Clearing, a division of Qucik & Reilly. "It had a runup in June, then bad sales in July so it broke down."
He said that the fact that overall sales (corrects from earnings) were up 19 percent was due to the opening of new stores.

An industry analyst who asked not to be named said that instead of marking down merchandise to boost sales in August, the company kept clothing prices stable during the month in order to maintain strong profits on the goods it did sell.
